rows.speaker: الكلبي والسدي ومقاتل وابن عباس في رواية عطاء
rows.claim: They say the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, called Akhnas because he withdrew with 300 men of Banu Zuhra from Badr; he charmed the Prophet, professed Islam and love, swore sincerity, and was a hypocrite inwardly.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬1) والسدي (¬2) ومقاتل (¬3) وابن عباس (¬4)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification in worldly life reflects his lying: the Prophet was not truly impressed with his words, and al-Akhnas earns no afterlife reward for them.
rows.anchor: لأنه كاذب، فما تعجب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من كلامه (¬8)

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He swears that he believes and loves the Prophet and claims God witnesses this inward faith, but he lies; the intended sense is faith in his own claim.
rows.anchor: فهو يحلف بالله ويشهده على أنه مضمر (¬2) ما يقوله، وهو كاذب

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Al-add means intensely quarrelsome; Abu Ishaq derives it from the two sides of the neck, since the man prevails whichever side of an argument he takes.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أخذ من لديدي العنق، وهما صفحتاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khisam is a verbal noun like mukhasama, from quarrelsomeness; disputation probes and constricts an issue, and vessel corners are called khusum, singular khasm.
rows.anchor: والخصام: مصدر، كالمخاصمة، والمخاصمة: مفاعلة من الخصومة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as a person who abandons the truth and argues for falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله: {ألد الخصام} يريد: الذي يدع الحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes his turning away as returning to Mecca: after leaving Badr with Banu Zuhra, al-Akhnas attacked Thaqif by night, killed their livestock, and burned their crops.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {وإذا تولى} يريد: راجعا إلى مكة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi gives another incident: al-Akhnas passed a Muslim field and donkeys, burned the field, and hamstrung the donkeys.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي. مر بزرع للمسلمين وحمر، فأحرق الزرع

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Mujahid read tawalla as gaining authority: when he governs, he acts unjustly; Ibn Abbas instead takes it as departing and turning away.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬5) ومجاهد (¬6): تولى بمعنى: ملك وولي

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the harvest as crops and plants and the progeny as livestock offspring, consistent with the report that he destroyed animals and burned crops.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن المراد بالحرث: الزرع والنبات، وبالنسل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that when a ruler acts through aggression and injustice, God withholds rain, so the drought destroys crops and livestock offspring.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إذا ولي فعمل بالعدوان والظلم أمسك الله المطر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the harvest as women and offspring as children; the author says this is soundly possible, citing the description of wives as a field.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الحرث: النساء، والنسل: الأولاد، وهذا غير مدفوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasl means offspring; its root may denote something emerging and falling out, as feathers, camel hair, or donkey hair shed, and a fallen piece is nusala.
rows.anchor: والنسل: معناه في اللغة: الولد، يقال: نسل بولد كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yansilun in the verse about people rushing to their Lord means hastening out; nasl is offspring because it emerges from the father's back and mother's womb.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله عز وجل: {إلى ربهم ينسلون} [يس: 51]، أي: يسرعون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in al-Kalbi's transmission, explains that God does not approve corruption or sinful acts.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي: أي: لا يرضى بالفساد والعمل بالمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption here has been glossed as ruin, clipping a coin, or tearing clothes when there is no beneficial purpose.
rows.anchor: وذكر في تفسير الفساد هاهنا: الخراب، وقطع الدرهم، وشق الثياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb and verbal noun vary as fasada/fasudan or fasadan, paralleling dhahaba/dhuhuban or dhahaban and kasada/kusudan or kasadan.
rows.anchor: ويقال: فسد الشيء يفسد فسودا وفسادا، كما يقال: ذهب ذهوبا وذهابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger called al-Akhnas to answer God inwardly and outwardly; arrogance and pride drew him toward sin and injustice.
rows.anchor: فدعاه الأنفة والكبر إلى الإثم والظلم، وهو قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-izza means invulnerability or force.
rows.anchor: ومعنى العزة هاهنا: المنعة والقوة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that when told to hold back, the man presses on more boldly in disobedience.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: إذا قيل له: مهلا مهلا ازداد إقداما على المعصية

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The people of linguistic interpretation say the pride carried, emboldened, or adorned the sin for him; taking someone by something can mean compelling him to it.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعانى: معنى (أخذته العزة بالإثم) حملته عليه، وجرأته عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is that pride and pre-Islamic zeal impelled him to commit sin.
rows.anchor: وتأويل الآية: حملته العزة وحمية الجاهلية على الفعل بالإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bi-l-ithm attaches to akhadhat, pride seized him through the sin he earned and led him to wrongdoing and lack of humility.
rows.anchor: والجار في قوله تعالى: {بالإثم} يجوز تعلقه بالأخذ وبالعزة، فإن علقته بالأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bi-l-ithm attaches to al-izza, it means taking pride in sin, which distances him from what God approves.
rows.anchor: وإن علقته بالعزة كان المعنى الاعتزاز بالإثم، أي: اعتز بما يؤثمه فيبعده مما يرضاه الله

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say Hell is sufficient for him as recompense and punishment; hasbuka dirham means one dirham suffices.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: كافيه الجحيم جزاء له وعذابا

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays's verse uses hasb in the sense of sufficiency: contentment and drinking one's fill suffice as wealth.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: وحسبك من غنى شبع وري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The triliteral form is obsolete; the quadriliteral ahsabani al-shayʾ means that something sufficed me.
rows.anchor: ويقال منه في الرباعي: أحسبني الشيء، إذا كفاني

rows.speaker: يونس وأكثر النحويين
rows.claim: Yunus and most grammarians say Jahannam is a foreign proper name for the afterlife's fire, indeclinable because of foreignness and definiteness.
rows.anchor: فقال يونس وأكثر النحويين: هي اسم للنار التي يعذب الله بها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say Jahannam is Arabic, named for the fire's deep bottom, and is indeclinable because it is definite and feminine.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: جهنم اسم عربي، سميت نار الآخرة بها لبعد قعرها

rows.speaker: قطرب عن رؤبة
rows.claim: Qutrub reports that Ruʾba called a deep well a jahnam.
rows.anchor: قال قطرب: حكي لنا عن رؤبة (¬4) أنه قال: ركية جهنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mihad is the plural of al-mahd, a place prepared for sleep; it derives from making something level, as a child's cradle or ground prepared for people.
rows.anchor: والمهاد: جمع المهد. والمهد: الموضع المهيأ للنوم، ومنه: مهد الصبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is called a bed as a fixed resting place, or because it replaces a bed for them, like the substitution in the cited phrase about glad tidings of painful punishment.
rows.anchor: الثبوت عليه، وقيل: لأنها بدل من المهاد لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mutallaqat are women released from their husbands' bonds; the verse concerns adult, consummated, nonpregnant divorcees whose waiting period is being explained.
rows.anchor: المطلقات: المخليات من حبال الأزواج (¬5) (¬6)، أراد المطلقات المدخول بهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must wait for three quruʾ to pass and not marry during that interval.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أنهن ينتظرن بأنفسهن (¬7) انقضاء ثلاثة قروء أو مضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is declarative in form but imperative in sense, as with the command that mothers nurse their children.
rows.anchor: لفظه خبر ومعناه الأمر، كقوله: {يرضعن أولادهن} [البقرة: 233]

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj compares the declarative command to saying a dirham suffices, whose intended force is to be content with a dirham.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: هو كما تقول: حسبك درهم، لفظه خبر ومعناه

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation supplies the ellipsis: they wait under God's ruling, which He made obligatory for them.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: معناه (¬1): يتربصن في حكم الله الذي أوجبه، فحذف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another grammatical explanation is that the lām of the imperative form ليتربصن has been omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد: ليتربصن، فحذف اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quruʾ is the plural of qarʾ; its few plural is aqruʾ, while its many plurals are aqraʾ and quruʾ.
rows.anchor: والقروء: جمع قرء (¬4)، وجمعه القليل أقرء، والكثير: أقراء وقروء

rows.speaker: يونس وأبو عمرو بن العلاء وأبو عبيد
rows.claim: Yunus, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala, and Abu Ubayd treat qarʾ as a word with opposite senses: menstruation and purity, in both Arabic usage and religious law.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يونس (¬6) وأبو عمرو بن العلاء (¬7) (¬8) وأبو عبيد أنها من الأضداد

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: The rajaz poet's line shows that quruʾ can mean menstrual periods.
rows.anchor: أنشد الأئمة حجة للحيض قول الراجز: له قروء كقروء الحائض

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line supports quruʾ meaning purity intervals: the man left on campaign and did not have intercourse with his wives.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا حجة للطهر قول الأعشى: ما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction to a woman with irregular bleeding to wait through her usual menstruation days and wash afterward shows that aqraʾ can mean menstruation.
rows.anchor: فقال (¬6) النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في المستحاضة "تنتظر (¬7) أيام أقرائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here quruʾ means three purity intervals: the command to divorce for the waiting period and the Prophet's instruction to Ibn Umar show divorce at purity so the waiting period begins prospectively.
rows.anchor: وأما استعمال الشرع إياها في الأطهار، فقوله تعالى: {يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word's two Arabic senses explain why Companions and jurists disagreed about the waiting period.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الاختلاف في اللغة وقع الخلاف في الأقراء بين الصحابة وفقهاء الأمة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says qarʾ means gathering: menstrual blood gathers in the womb, and this gathering occurs during purity.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: والذي عندي في حقيقة هذا أن القرء الجمع (¬8) في اللغة

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says three quruʾ is irregular: the measure should be three aqruʾ, because quruʾ is the many plural, as three aflus precedes fulus.
rows.anchor: ذكر أبو حاتم عن الأصمعي أنه قال في قوله: {ثلاثة قروء}: جاء هذا

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim says grammarians understand an omitted partitive phrase: three of the quruʾ.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: وقال النحويون في هذا: أراد ثلاثة من القروء

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The people of linguistic interpretation explain the many plural as signaling that this rule applies to numerous divorcees, though each is assigned three at a time.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: لما كانت كل مطلقة يلزمها (¬8) هذا، دخله معنى الكثرة

rows.speaker: من قال إن القرء حيض
rows.claim: Those who take qarʾ as menstruation say a woman does not leave her waiting period until her third menstrual period has ended.
rows.anchor: فمن قال: القرء: الحيض، قال: لا تخرج المرأة من عدتها ما لم

rows.speaker: من قال إن القرء الأطهار
rows.claim: Those who take quruʾ as purity say a divorce during menstruation does not count the partial interval, while divorce during purity counts its remainder as one interval followed by two complete ones.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: إنها الأطهار، قال: إن طلقها في خلال الحيض لم يحتسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The womb is the place where a child originates and the vessel that holds it in the abdomen.
rows.anchor: الرحم: منبت الولد ووعاؤه في البطن

rows.speaker: عكرمة وإبراهيم
rows.claim: Ikrima and Ibrahim interpret what is in the womb as menstruation, in the case of a woman claiming her third period has passed to prevent her husband from returning.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة (¬3) وإبراهيم (¬4): يعنى: الحيض، وهو أن تكون المرأة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Muqatil interpret it as pregnancy and the child; concealment could defeat a husband's right of return or the child's rights.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬5) وقتادة (¬6) ومقاتل (¬7): يعنى: الحبل والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers pregnancy and the child because what God creates in wombs points more directly to a child than to menstruation.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أولى؛ لأن قوله: {ما خلق الله في أرحامهن} أدل على الولد

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that a wicked wife may conceal pregnancy because she longs for her husband and wants to prolong the waiting period; a pregnant woman's period ends at childbirth.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولا يحل لهن} الآية، وذلك أن المرأة السوء

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means that a believer is expected to act this way; the obligation is not limited to believers alone.
rows.anchor: معناه: من كان مؤمنا (¬3) بالله واليوم الآخر (¬4) فهذه صفته

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq compares it to telling a wrongdoer that if he is a believer he should not wrong the speaker; faith should restrain the wrong.
rows.anchor: قال (¬5) أبو إسحاق: وهذا كما تقول للرجل يظلم (¬6): إن كنت مؤمنا فلا تظلم

words: وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women must disclose what is in their wombs, since only they know it; concealment is sinful betrayal, a plausible declaration is accepted, and a suspected woman must swear an oath.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية أمر متوجه على النساء في إظهار ما يخلق (¬8) الله في أرحامهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿula is a collective plural of baʿl, like fuḥula, dhukura, khuʾula, and ʿumuma; its feminine tāʾ reinforces the group's grammatical femininity and is only used in attested forms.
rows.anchor: البعولة: جمع بعل، كالفحولة والذكورة والخؤولة والعمومة، وهذه الهاء

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Baʿula is also the verbal noun of baʿala, becoming a husband, as Yaʿqub's poetic line uses the verb.
rows.anchor: والبعولة أيضا: مصدر البعل، يقال: بعل الرجل يبعل بعولة

rows.speaker: الحطيئة
rows.claim: Baʿal and tubāʿil can refer to intercourse or a husband's play with his wife; al-Hutayʾa uses tubāʿil in a line about a wife.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا يقال (¬5) للجماع وملاعبة الرجل أهله: بعال، يقال للمرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman praised for good tabaʿʿul treats her husband well; the author also cites a hadith about women excelling in their treatment of husbands.
rows.anchor: وامرأة حسنة التبعل: إذا كانت تحسن عشرة زوجها. ومنه الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their husbands have the stronger right to restore them to marriage during the period in which they have been commanded to wait.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {أحق بردهن}، أي: إلى النكاح والزوجية، يعني: أحق بمراجعتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition excludes harm: in pre-Islamic practice a husband repeatedly divorced and returned his wife near the end of each waiting period to prolong her distress; return is allowed for reconciliation.
rows.anchor: {إن أرادوا إصلاحا} لا إضرارا، وذلك أن الرجل في الجاهلية إذا أراد الإضرار بامرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband may revoke without a guardian, her consent, or a newly specified dowry; the remaining waiting period ends and intercourse is immediately lawful, with witnesses recommended as a precaution and return expressed by words such as I have returned you.
rows.anchor: ويستغني الزوج في المراجعة عن الولي وعن رضاها وعن تسمية مهر، وإذا راجعها سقطت بقية العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women have rights over men comparable to the rights men have over them, in the recognized manner and under the duties God has prescribed.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف} أي: للنساء على الرجال مثل الذي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he adorns himself for his wife just as she adorns herself for him, citing the verse's reciprocity.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: إني لأتزين لامرأتي كما تتزين لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root associations of rajul and related forms indicate strength: a powerful man or horse, forceful speech, and daylight gaining strength.
rows.anchor: يقال: رجل بين الرجلة (¬3)، أي: القوة، وهو أرجل الرجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daraja means rank or level and derives from progressing, folding, or passing away step by step; a road's passage is also called a madraja.
rows.anchor: والدرجة: المنزلة، وأصلها من درجت الشيء أدرجه درجا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains men's degree as the dowry they provide and the money they spend on their wives.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر، وأنفق عليها من المال (¬4)

rows.speaker: قيل بالعقل
rows.claim: One reported explanation says the degree is men's greater reason or intellect.
rows.anchor: وأما المعنى (¬3) فقال ابن عباس: بما ساق إليها من المهر، وأنفق عليها من المال (¬4). وقيل: بالعقل

rows.speaker: قيل بالدية
rows.claim: Another reported explanation says the degree concerns blood money.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالعقل. وقيل: بالدية. وقيل: بالميراث

rows.speaker: قيل بالميراث
rows.claim: Another reported explanation says the degree concerns inheritance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالدية. وقيل: بالميراث (¬5). وقال قتادة: بالجهاد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains men's degree as jihad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالميراث (¬5). وقال قتادة: بالجهاد

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says women receive pleasure from men as men do from women, while men have the advantage of providing maintenance and care.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: المعنى: أن المرأة تنال من اللذة من الرجل، كما ينال الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sovereign, commands and tests as He wills, and does so only with profound wisdom.
rows.anchor: أي: مالك يأمر كما أراد، ويمتحن كما أحب، ولا يكون ذلك إلا عن حكمة بالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected wording would address the two spouses as fa-in khāfā, matching the preceding clause; Hamza reads fa-in khīfā, matching his dual reading of yakhāfā, but the plural is also justified.
rows.anchor: كان من حق النظم أن يكون فإن خافا (يعنى الزوجين، ليشاكل قوله: {إلا أن يخافا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is a shift from third-person dual to plural address, as in the cited transition in 30:39; the dual pronoun denotes any couple in this situation.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون انصرف من الغيبة إلى الخطاب كما قال: {وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plural addresses rulers and jurists responsible for the public, after the passage shifts from addressing everyone to the two spouses and then combines them with the public addressees.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أن قوله: (فإن خفتم) خطاب (¬1) لولاة الأمر والفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line likewise begins by addressing one person, shifts to a plural command, and then uses the dual.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا النظم قد جاء في الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear means knowing or strongly judging that the spouses will not maintain God's limits in good companionship; then the wife may ransom herself from her husband without blame.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {فإن خفتم ألا} أي: علمتم وغلب على ظنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the main relief is for a husband taking the ransom, both are named so the wife is not mistaken for a sinful squanderer of money; the author points to a similar phrase elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال: {فلا جناح عليهما} والمقصود رفع الحرج عن الزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of fear is omitted because it is evident: the threat is an enemy.
rows.anchor: أراد خفتم عدوا فحذف المفعول لإحاطه العلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijāl is a plural of rājil like tājir/tujjār; a rājil is someone on foot, whether walking or standing, and it has several plural forms.
rows.anchor: والرجال: جمع راجل، مثل: تاجر وتجار، وصاحب وصحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukbān is the plural of rākib, parallel to fāris/fursān.
rows.anchor: والركبان: جمع راكب، مثل: فارس وفرسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If you cannot pray standing and fulfill prayer's full due, pray walking on foot or riding; this suffices.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: فإن لم يمكنكم أن تصلوا قانتين موفين للصلاة حقها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes describe prayer amid sword fighting or pursuit: face the qibla if possible, otherwise not; pronounce the takbir, recite, gesture for bowing and prostration, keep the rakah count, and shorten if traveling.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: هذا في المسايفة والمطاردة، يكبر الرجل مستقبل القبلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly says the Prophet prescribed four rakahs at home, two while traveling, and one in fear; the author says this is a school position that is not acted upon.
rows.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: فرض الله على لسان نبيكم الصلاة في الحضر أربعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is prayer in extreme fear, when a person may pray mounted, gesture, and face any direction; the separate prayer of fear is discussed in Surat al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: وهذه صلاة شدة الخوف، وهي التي يجوز للمصلي أن يصلي

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar glosses the verse as allowing prayer facing the qibla or not facing it.
rows.anchor: وقال (¬2) ابن عمر في تفسير هذه الآية: ومستقبلي القبلة وغير مستقبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extreme-fear gesture prayer also applies to danger from a predator, flood, charging camel, or other likely peril; a person may gesture and run if the prayer time may be missed.
rows.anchor: والصلاة بالإيماء في شدة الخوف لا يختص (¬3) بخوف المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When safe, pray the five prayers in full and fulfill their due requirements.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فإذا أمنتم فاذكروا الله} فصلوا الصلوات الخمس تامة

words: كَمَا عَلَّمَكُم مَّا لَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's teaching here means that He prescribed the prayers at their appointed times.
rows.anchor: {كما علمكم ما لم تكونوا تعلمون} يريد: كما افترض عليكم في مواقيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns everything in the heavens and earth, including its entities, disposal, and governance.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى {ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض} وهو مالك أعيانه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية مقسم ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in transmissions from Muqsim and Mujahid, says the verse concerns witnesses who disclose or conceal testimony; al-Shaʿbi and Ikrima hold the same view.
rows.anchor: اختلف الروايات عن ابن عباس في معنى هذه الآية، فقال في رواية مقسم ومجاهد (¬2)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in transmissions from Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Ata, says the verse was abrogated: Companions feared involuntary thoughts, the Prophet urged them to say we hear and obey, and after a year the relief of 2:286 came.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية سعيد بن جبير (¬3) وعطاء (¬4): هذه الآية منسوخة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said God has pardoned his community for thoughts that arise within themselves unless they act on them or speak them aloud.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: "إن الله تجاوز لأمتي ما حدثوا به أنفسهم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة والقرظي وابن سيرين والكلبي وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Abu Hurayra, al-Qurazi, Ibn Sirin, al-Kalbi, and Qatada also hold that the earlier verse was abrogated.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن مسعود (¬3) وأبي هريرة (¬4) والقرظي (¬5) وابن سيرين (¬6)

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak indicates that the verse remains operative: deliberate, resolved inward acts are accountable, but unchosen passing thoughts are not; heart actions are real earnings, as other verses show.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية الضحاك (¬1) ما يدل على أن الآية محكمة غير منسوخة

rows.speaker: الحسن والربيع
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Rabiʿ share the view that unintentional thoughts that are not resolved are not among what God charges a person to bear.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول الحسن (¬4) والربيع (¬5)

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takallafa means to impose a burden; takalluf is the verb, and kulfa is the noun.
rows.anchor: يقال: كلفته الشيء فتكلف، والكلفة الاسم منه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says wusʿ is a noun like wajd and jahd, meaning what a person can accommodate without being squeezed or burdened.
rows.anchor: والوسع، قال الفراء: هو اسم، كالوجد والجهد

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and most exegetes say this verse abrogated the burden of involuntary thoughts and whispers imposed by the earlier verse.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس (¬4) وأكثر المفسرين على أن هذه الآية نسخت ما ضج المؤمنون عنه

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another transmission, Ibn Abbas says God imposed only what believers can do, citing God's desire for ease, removal of hardship, and the command to fear Him as able.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه من طريق آخر، أنه قال: معناه: أنه كلف المؤمنين ما هم له مستطيعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best explanation is that capacity here is below full ability: God graciously burdens people with less than their maximum; Sufyan ibn Uyayna glosses it as ease, since a full-capacity burden would exhaust them.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن ما قيل في (¬1) تفسير هذه الآية (¬2)، وذلك أن الوسع دون الطاقة

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: The Qadari objection is that if God decrees someone's disbelief yet commands faith, He has burdened that person with what is beyond his capacity.
rows.anchor: وتقول القدرية: إن الله تعالى أخبر أنه لا يكلف العبد إلا ما يسعه

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the same objection applies to foreknowledge: if God's prior knowledge says someone will die an unbeliever, that person cannot change it; al-Shafiʿi says the Qadari are defeated if they concede foreknowledge.
rows.anchor: فيقال لهم: يلزمكم مثل هذا في العلم، لأنكم توافقوننا على أن الله تعالى إذا سبق

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correct linguistic view is that kasb and iktisab are synonymous; Dhu al-Rumma uses both forms for earning in one line.
rows.anchor: الصحيح عند أهل اللغة: أن الكسب والاكتساب واحد، لا فرق بينهما

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say iktisab is narrower: kasb may benefit oneself or another, while iktisab is only for oneself; one can be a provider for family but not an iktisab-earner for them.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الاكتساب أخص من الكسب؛ لأن الكسب ينقسم إلى كسبه لنفسه

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person is accountable for their own earnings and is not punished for another person's sin.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت} أي: لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes the prayer opening as an instruction: say, Our Lord.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ربنا لا تؤاخذنا} قال الحسن: معناه: قولوا: ربنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation treats it as reported speech: they say, Our Lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي: يقولون: ربنا. على الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La tuʾakhidhna means do not punish us.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {لا تؤاخذنا}: لا تعاقبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal verb is used though punishment has one agent: the sinner exposes himself and opens the way through his own deed, as if helping the punisher seize him.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاء بلفظ المفاعلة وهو فعل واحد؛ لأن المسيء قد أمكن من نفسه
